[LNUL.5.4] **Narrowing is exactly two mechanical cases** — the flow-typing
boundary that holds the "small `dsc` lift, no inference engine" promise.
Narrowing of a `T?` to `T` occurs in **exactly two** cases: (a) the tail of a
`where` conjunction after an `x is not null and` guard, where `x` is `T` in the
remaining conjuncts ([LNUL.5.2]); and (b) the result of `x ?? d` (`d : T`), which
is `T` ([LNUL.5.3]). **No other construct narrows** — not `or`, not
`not (x is null)`, not a prior `let`, not nested or cross-rule flow. The
consequence of *not* narrowing is **position-dependent** ([LNUL.5.1]): a `T?`
outside a narrowing site is a compile error in a concrete-value position, and
Kleene-evaluated (null-propagating) in a `where`-predicate. So `s.state is null or
s.state > 85` **compiles**: `s.state` is still `T?` at `> 85`, but a comparison in
a `where` propagates `null` ([LNUL.4.1]), so with a `null` reading `s.state is
null` is `true` and `true or null` is `true` (Kleene) — the rule **fires**. That
is a *semantic* gotcha, not a compile error: the `or` did not narrow, so the
intended guard silently didn't apply. An author who wants "hot, treating a missing
reading as not-hot" writes `(s.state ?? 0.0) > 85` or `s.state is not null and
s.state > 85`. The cost is an occasional explicit guard a cleverer compiler would
infer — the deliberate price of a fully predictable, two-case narrowing model with
no data-flow-analysis subsystem in `dsc`.

**The guards are spelled with `is` throughout.** `!= null` and `== null` are
compile errors ([LNUL.4.4]). Narrowing is keyed on the **total** null test and
never on the propagating comparison.

alloy.name: lnul_5_4__v5_false_decides
alloy.note: NARROWING: a false anywhere decides whatever the rest would raise, and nothing is recorded -- so folding a literal false operand is sound (RLOW.6.1.4). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_5_4__false_decides
idris.note: NARROWING: a false guard decides the `where` wherever it stands, whatever any other conjunct -- the guarded tail included -- would raise, and nothing is recorded: [IRET.9.6]'s narrowed tail evaluated before its guard meets a `false` guard that absorbs its TypeError. And folding a literal `false` operand is sound (RLOW.6.1.4). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.
